rationale: Record a Pulp-owned `pulp doctor` diagnostic that reports stale git lock files. A `*.lock` left behind by a process that died fails every index- and ref-writing git command in a checkout while reads keep working, so the checkout looks healthy and only writes are dead; two real instances in this repository went unnoticed for nine and fifty-three days. The new row reports a lock only when it exists, no live process holds it, and it is older than an hour, and its remediation is prose rather than an argv so `--fix` declines to execute it. The watched surface this touches is `docs/status/cli-commands.yaml`, edited solely to document that new doctor row as the repository's CLI docs rule requires; the rest of the change is `tools/cli` doctor helpers plus its test. It adds no import, packaging, or release-artifact behavior, does not alter design import, generic rendering primitives, or any packaging or CLI-installation path in this family, and does not touch Vellum source authority.
tests: pulp-test-cli-git-lock-health (stale, held-lock control, real lsof probe, worktree and probe-budget coverage)
